data.one_liner: Pure Dart cryptographic, encoding, and blockchain toolkit for addresses, keys, and mnemonics.
data.what_it_does: Provides a comprehensive set of cryptographic algorithms, data encoding formats (Base58, Bech32, CBOR, etc.), blockchain address management, and hierarchical deterministic key derivation standards (BIP32, BIP39, SLIP10) entirely in pure Dart.
use_when: You need to generate or manage BIP39/SLIP10 mnemonics and derive cryptographic keys.
You need to encode, decode, or validate various blockchain addresses (Bitcoin, Ethereum, Substrate, Solana, etc.).
You require cross-platform cryptographic primitives and hashing functions without external dependencies.
avoid_when: You need high-level blockchain RPC client integrations rather than low-level crypto and address primitives.
You require hardware wallet bindings natively managed via platform USB/Bluetooth bridges.
strengths: Zero external dependencies, making it highly portable and lightweight.
Extensive support for multi-curve key derivation and dozens of blockchain address types.
Pure Dart implementation works seamlessly across mobile, web, and desktop platforms.
weaknesses: Not an all-in-one smart contract interaction library (does not include full JSON-RPC node provider implementations for every chain).
Manual handling of low-level crypto operations requires strong domain knowledge.
data.setup_notes: No native dependencies or build_runner steps required since it is written in pure Dart.

alternatives.name: web3dart
alternatives.why_pick_it: Pick web3dart if you specifically need a complete Ethereum wallet and smart contract interaction library.

alternatives.name: bip39
alternatives.why_pick_it: Pick bip39 if you only need lightweight BIP39 mnemonic generation without the massive multi-blockchain and multi-curve toolkit.
